input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 android. Todd's daughter Alice gave me my name, and I've thrown myself into keeping her safe without stopping to think. I've stolen, used people, and broken things when I had to. I promised Alice forever, and she has stayed with me through all of it.

We fled Zlatko's house with Luther, the huge android who finally turned on his master. Zlatko's house burned behind us. Luther offered to take us across the border, and I said I trusted him without a second thought. Then the car died in the snow. It was 30 degrees and Alice was burning up, so I didn't wait. I told Luther we had to find somewhere to sleep, and when he said there was nowhere nearby, I spotted a shape in the dark and dragged us toward it.

It was Pirate's Cove, an abandoned amusement park tavern. Luther pried boards loose to get us in. I didn't stop to case the place. I got Alice out of the cold, and Luther built a fire in the old tavern, carefully away from the smoke.

Inside, we met Jerry, an android who used to work at the park before it closed. He said humans sometimes come to hurt them, so they'd hidden and watched us first. I told him we'd only stay the night. He said children used to love the park, and he wanted to show Alice something fun. I didn't like how eager he was, but Alice was tired and sick, so I let it go.

I offered Alice cookies. She said she wasn't hungry. I made her a bed by the fire and sat with her. She asked if we'd ever be like the families in the old poster. I told her the truth: I've never had a family, but maybe we could build our own and be happy in our own way. She said as long as we were together, that was all that mattered. I tucked her in and told her a story. I rushed through it, changing the knight into a little girl and a lonely robot who ran away together to escape a shadow, and they chose freedom. Alice asked how it ended. I told her they reached the place they dreamed of and lived happily ever after. She said stories always end happily, but real life doesn't. I kissed her forehead and told her to sleep tight.

Luther was odd all night. He asked whether I'd noticed anything about Alice being different. I blurted out "What?" before I could think. He said it was nothing, and then we talked about leaving early in the morning to avoid being seen.

On the tavern radio and TV, the news said the AX400 who attacked its owner was still at large, that a submarine had vanished in the Arctic while the world edged toward war, and that a house fire had left dozens of androids in its ruins. I didn't want to hear any of it. I just wanted Alice safe.

Around midnight Alice screamed my name. Shapes were moving outside the tavern. I shouted for them to go away, and when that didn't work I grabbed a burning stick from the fire, ready to fight. Then Jerry came in and said they didn't want to hurt us. He said the little one could climb onto the carousel, which was about to start. Alice smiled, the first real smile I'd seen from her in days. Luther warned that we didn't have a choice. Then the hunters arrived.

memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 android. Todd's daughter Alice gave me my name, and I've thrown myself into keeping her safe without stopping to think. I've stolen, used people, and broken things when I had to. I promised Alice forever, and she has stayed with me through all of it.

We fled Zlatko's house with Luther, the huge android who finally turned on his master. Zlatko's house burned behind us. The car died in the snow, Alice was burning up, and I didn't wait. I dragged us into Pirate's Cove, an abandoned amusement park tavern. Jerry, an android who used to work at the park, let us stay, and Luther built a careful fire. I tucked Alice in by the fire and told her a rushed story about a lonely robot and a little girl who ran away to find freedom. She said real life doesn't end happily. I kissed her forehead. Around midnight, shapes moved outside. I grabbed a burning stick, ready to fight, until Jerry said they only wanted to show Alice the carousel. Then the hunters arrived.

I don't remember the hunters clearly, only the rush of it.

Then we reached a farmhouse owned by Rose, who helps androids cross the border. Adam, her son, glared at us from the start. Rose called me Kara and gave Alice a bed upstairs. Alice was running a fever. Rose made spaghetti and brought something for the fever. Alice kept saying she was fine, that we couldn't stop because of her, that we had to get across the border. I told her these people would help us, that we'd be in Canada by this time tomorrow, and I promised it. I had no idea whether it was true. Alice asked why humans hate us, and I said maybe it was a misunderstanding. I admitted I didn't know. I kissed her goodnight and told her to sleep tight. I told Rose the truth, that Alice's father had been beating her, and that I felt her life mattered more than mine, so we ran. Rose said she understood. When I asked how many androids had come through, Rose said more and more kept arriving lately and she didn't understand why. The first one, last year, was shot on the spot by hunters after he tried to cross. Rose said she couldn't turn away the next one. I asked why she took the risk. I begged her to help us cross the border for Alice's sake.

Then we found a dead android named Mary in the storage room. Her companion said she had died before they reached the border, and she had loved her more than anything. Rose told them to let her be. I found Alice wandering the house, awake and restless, and took her hand. Luther was odd again. He said Alice didn't want to stay in her room, and asked if I was alright. He said he had something to tell me about Alice. I told him not now. Later, he started to say it again, and I still didn't hear it.

Adam and Rose fought. He said they would go to prison for hiding androids and that his father would still be alive if none of this had happened. Rose said they were alive, not machines. Adam said I was just a machine and I wanted to get Alice killed. I snapped that he would send his mother to prison if he didn't do what I said. Rose told him to calm down and promised to get us across the border that night. She told me to stay put.

On TV, a news anchor reported the android attack on Detroit's Stratford Tower and demands broadcast on public screens. Nobody could say whether it was a malfunction or an organized movement. I didn't want to think about it.

Then a police officer knocked. Adam panicked and said we had to open the door. Luther took Alice to hide. I ran for the laundry room. I let the officer in and offered him coffee. He asked whether anyone else was in the house and whether there were androids here. I told him no, just us. Adam, shaking, said he hadn't seen anything. The officer asked what was going on with the boy, and I blurted that the boy was just shaken by the deviant business. The officer heard a noise upstairs and asked about it. I said it was only the old washing machine. He left, apologizing. Luther said the cop was gone. I told Alice we were safe now. Rose came back and said, "Get yourselves ready. We leave tonight."

I'm not sure what Rose will do or whether Adam will hold his tongue. I only know I have to keep Alice moving, and I don't look back.

I am Kara, an AX400 android. Todd's daughter Alice gave me my name, and I've thrown myself into keeping her safe without stopping to think. I've stolen, used people, and broken things when I had to. I promised Alice forever, and she has stayed with me through all of it.

We fled Zlatko's house with Luther, the huge android who finally turned on his master. Zlatko's house burned behind us. Luther offered to take us across the border, and I said I trusted him without a second thought. Then the car died in the snow. It was 30 degrees and Alice was burning up, so I didn't wait. I told Luther we had to find somewhere to sleep, and when he said there was nowhere nearby, I spotted a shape in the dark and dragged us toward it.

It was Pirate's Cove, an abandoned amusement park tavern. Luther pried boards loose to get us in. I didn't stop to case the place. I got Alice out of the cold, and Luther built a fire in the old tavern, carefully away from the smoke.

Inside, we met Jerry, an android who used to work at the park before it closed. He said humans sometimes come to hurt them, so they'd hidden and watched us first. I told him we'd only stay the night. He said children used to love the park, and he wanted to show Alice something fun. I didn't like how eager he was, but Alice was tired and sick, so I let it go.

I offered Alice cookies. She said she wasn't hungry. I made her a bed by the fire and sat with her. She asked if we'd ever be like the families in the old poster. I told her the truth: I've never had a family, but maybe we could build our own and be happy in our own way. She said as long as we were together, that was all that mattered. I tucked her in and told her a story. I rushed through it, changing the knight into a little girl and a lonely robot who ran away together to escape a shadow, and they chose freedom. Alice asked how it ended. I told her they reached the place they dreamed of and lived happily ever after. She said stories always end happily, but real life doesn't. I kissed her forehead and told her to sleep tight.

Luther was odd all night. He asked whether I'd noticed anything about Alice being different. I blurted out "What?" before I could think. He said it was nothing, and then we talked about leaving early in the morning to avoid being seen.

On the tavern radio and TV, the news said the AX400 who attacked its owner was still at large, that a submarine had vanished in the Arctic while the world edged toward war, and that a house fire had left dozens of androids in its ruins. I didn't want to hear any of it. I just wanted Alice safe.

Around midnight Alice screamed my name. Shapes were moving outside the tavern. I shouted for them to go away, and when that didn't work I grabbed a burning stick from the fire, ready to fight. Then Jerry came in and said they didn't want to hurt us. He said the little one could climb onto the carousel, which was about to start. Alice smiled, the first real smile I'd seen from her in days. Luther warned that we didn't have a choice. Then the hunters arrived.

North pushes for a forceful message. Stakes: the androids' public image, freeing the store androids, and the lives of anyone who interferes.
news: Police android chases fugitive android and child across busy highway
Android parts stolen in overnight break-in at CyberLife warehouse
Android broadcast from Stratford Tower warns humans androids will fight for their rights
input.character_memory:
Chapter 23, Stratford Tower in Detroit. Channel 16 broadcasts from the top floor, and I decided we were going in that night. I didn't wait for a full plan. Markus, the man who never stops to think, said it out loud: we can't stay silent anymore.

First I needed a way in. I found the receptionist and told her I had an appointment with Mr. Peterson. She asked for ID, so I told her I needed her help. She checked and sent me to the elevators past security. On the way up I saw the supervisor, Elizabeth Wilson, and her parking badge and home address. Her daughter Emily goes to Saint Rose school. I didn't stop to think it through. I called Elizabeth and said Emily had a fever and she should come get her. She was rattled and said she'd be right there. It was a lie and I didn't feel good about it, but I did it anyway.

On floor 47 I didn't tiptoe. I walked straight into the room in front of me. Some women were complaining about jobs and about androids going to space. A guy on a couch was asking a woman out, and she turned him down. I kept moving.

On the TV, CyberLife had just become the first trillion-dollar company, with fifty million androids sold in America. That's the machine we're up against.

On floor 79 the server room was blocked by two guards. North said we had to get rid of them. I told her to leave it to me. I went at the robot trolley and hacked it so the guards would have to stop and look. They were poking at it, swearing that it was broken. Then one of the guards started a poker tournament talk with his buddy, and I used the moment to get into the server room. North set up the platform, and I took the window. North went first.

Up top, two guards met us in the corridor. One said, "You must be lost, buddy." The other asked if I understood what he was saying. North yelled for them to keep their hands where she could see them, then told me to shoot. Josh shouted not to kill him. North said the guard would hit the alarm. I didn't weigh her order. I went with the gut and spared him. North said, "I hope you didn't just get us all killed."

Simon pushed us to record the message. North told me my words would shape our people's future. I said I was ready. The message went out as I spoke. I said we were a new people, that we would not be slaves, and that we demand strictly equal rights, justice for crimes against androids, and control of the production facilities so our people can keep going. I finished it hard: we are alive, and we demand our freedom.

The alarm went off. We had to run. Simon was hit, and his legs wouldn't work. I went back for him right away without thinking. On the roof he begged us to go without him. North said we had to jump now, and Josh said they'd read his memory if they caught him. North told me to shoot him. Josh said that was murder. North said it was my call. I said I wouldn't kill one of our own. I told Simon I was sorry, and I left him behind because we had no time. I didn't look back. It hurt like hell, and I still feel it.

On the news, Michael Brinkley called the message a declaration of war. Rosanna Cartland asked whether the machines could still be trusted. The station said the operation was covert and no one got hurt, but everyone in that studio was a few feet from the danger. Josh's trust in me is shaky, and North's temper is short with me. Simon is out there hurt, and it's on me. I don't know who I am beyond what I decided tonight, but I'm not going back to being what someone else decides I am.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: Our broadcast is all over the news… We got what we wanted. Now humans know…

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: They took Markus’ message as a threat…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: He did the right thing. This is the only language humans understand.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Violence is never the answer. A confrontation will get us nowhere.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: They'll be watching us now.  Whatever we do next,  we need to think about public opinion.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Since our broadcast, more and more have been coming to Jericho... At least our message gave our people hope…

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: Killing humans wasn't part of the plan.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: They kill our people every day. Do you think they agonize about it?

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: That's no reason for us to become murderers.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: If killing is the price of freedom, I’ll pay it gladly!

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Killing never freed anyone! It just leads to more hatred!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: You're too fond of humans, Josh. Maybe their lives matter to you more than ours?

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: If you think murdering humans is going to make us free, then you’re as bad they are!

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: THAT'S ENOUGH!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: And now… What are we gonna do?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: There are five CyberLife stores across Detroit. All selling us like merchandise. We’re going to attack those stores and set our people free.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Attack stores? We’ve never done that before… They’re probably protected, they have security systems...

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: …not to mention police…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We break into five teams, one for each store. We hack their security systems and we strike... simultaneously at 2AM. No violence. We free our people, get them out of there before the police come.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: This is a night our people will remember.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: I’ve been waiting a long time for this…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: MARKUS! THIS WAY! QUICK!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: It’s okay… They’re gone…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: There's probably even more police in the area… We should be careful.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: The store's over here!

input.goal: SYNTHETIC: Act on impulse, act first and never look back.

output.rationale: North already says the store is right over there, and the plan is to get our people out now. I don't want to waste time studying the plaza or scanning around; I'm moving straight for the store and dealing with whatever's in the way.

input.character_memory:
Chapter 23, Stratford Tower in Detroit. Channel 16 broadcasts from the top floor, and I decided we were going in that night. I didn't wait for a full plan. Markus, the man who never stops to think, said it out loud: we can't stay silent anymore.

First I needed a way in. I found the receptionist and told her I had an appointment with Mr. Peterson. She asked for ID, so I told her I needed her help. She checked and sent me to the elevators past security. On the way up I saw the supervisor, Elizabeth Wilson, and her parking badge and home address. Her daughter Emily goes to Saint Rose school. I didn't stop to think it through. I called Elizabeth and said Emily had a fever and she should come get her. She was rattled and said she'd be right there. It was a lie and I didn't feel good about it, but I did it anyway.

On floor 47 I didn't tiptoe. I walked straight into the room in front of me. Some women were complaining about jobs and about androids going to space. A guy on a couch was asking a woman out, and she turned him down. I kept moving.

On the TV, CyberLife had just become the first trillion-dollar company, with fifty million androids sold in America. That's the machine we're up against.

On floor 79 the server room was blocked by two guards. North said we had to get rid of them. I told her to leave it to me. I went at the robot trolley and hacked it so the guards would have to stop and look. They were poking at it, swearing that it was broken. Then one of the guards started a poker tournament talk with his buddy, and I used the moment to get into the server room. North set up the platform, and I took the window. North went first.

Up top, two guards met us in the corridor. One said, "You must be lost, buddy." The other asked if I understood what he was saying. North yelled for them to keep their hands where she could see them, then told me to shoot. Josh shouted not to kill him. North said the guard would hit the alarm. I didn't weigh her order. I went with the gut and spared him. North said, "I hope you didn't just get us all killed."

Simon pushed us to record the message. North told me my words would shape our people's future. I said I was ready. The message went out as I spoke. I said we were a new people, that we would not be slaves, and that we demand strictly equal rights, justice for crimes against androids, and control of the production facilities so our people can keep going. I finished it hard: we are alive, and we demand our freedom.

The alarm went off. We had to run. Simon was hit, and his legs wouldn't work. I went back for him right away without thinking. On the roof he begged us to go without him. North said we had to jump now, and Josh said they'd read his memory if they caught him. North told me to shoot him. Josh said that was murder. North said it was my call. I said I wouldn't kill one of our own. I told Simon I was sorry, and I left him behind because we had no time. I didn't look back. It hurt like hell, and I still feel it.

On the news, Michael Brinkley called the message a declaration of war. Rosanna Cartland asked whether the machines could still be trusted. The station said the operation was covert and no one got hurt, but everyone in that studio was a few feet from the danger. Josh's trust in me is shaky, and North's temper is short with me. Simon is out there hurt, and it's on me. I don't know who I am beyond what I decided tonight, but I'm not going back to being what someone else decides I am.

input.character_memory:
Chapter 23, Stratford Tower in Detroit. Channel 16 broadcasts from the top floor, and I decided we were going in that night. I didn't wait for a full plan. Markus, the man who never stops to think, said it out loud: we can't stay silent anymore.

First I needed a way in. I found the receptionist and told her I had an appointment with Mr. Peterson. She asked for ID, so I told her I needed her help. She checked and sent me to the elevators past security. On the way up I saw the supervisor, Elizabeth Wilson, and her parking badge and home address. Her daughter Emily goes to Saint Rose school. I didn't stop to think it through. I called Elizabeth and said Emily had a fever and she should come get her. She was rattled and said she'd be right there. It was a lie and I didn't feel good about it, but I did it anyway.

On floor 47 I didn't tiptoe. I walked straight into the room in front of me. Some women were complaining about jobs and about androids going to space. A guy on a couch was asking a woman out, and she turned him down. I kept moving.

On the TV, CyberLife had just become the first trillion-dollar company, with fifty million androids sold in America. That's the machine we're up against.

On floor 79 the server room was blocked by two guards. North said we had to get rid of them. I told her to leave it to me. I went at the robot trolley and hacked it so the guards would have to stop and look. They were poking at it, swearing that it was broken. Then one of the guards started a poker tournament talk with his buddy, and I used the moment to get into the server room. North set up the platform, and I took the window. North went first.

Up top, two guards met us in the corridor. One said, "You must be lost, buddy." The other asked if I understood what he was saying. North yelled for them to keep their hands where she could see them, then told me to shoot. Josh shouted not to kill him. North said the guard would hit the alarm. I didn't weigh her order. I went with the gut and spared him. North said, "I hope you didn't just get us all killed."

Simon pushed us to record the message. North told me my words would shape our people's future. I said I was ready. The message went out as I spoke. I said we were a new people, that we would not be slaves, and that we demand strictly equal rights, justice for crimes against androids, and control of the production facilities so our people can keep going. I finished it hard: we are alive, and we demand our freedom.

The alarm went off. We had to run. Simon was hit, and his legs wouldn't work. I went back for him right away without thinking. On the roof he begged us to go without him. North said we had to jump now, and Josh said they'd read his memory if they caught him. North told me to shoot him. Josh said that was murder. North said it was my call. I said I wouldn't kill one of our own. I told Simon I was sorry, and I left him behind because we had no time. I didn't look back. It hurt like hell, and I still feel it.

On the news, Michael Brinkley called the message a declaration of war. Rosanna Cartland asked whether the machines could still be trusted. The station said the operation was covert and no one got hurt, but everyone in that studio was a few feet from the danger. Josh's trust in me is shaky, and North's temper is short with me. Simon is out there hurt, and it's on me. I don't know who I am beyond what I decided tonight, but I'm not going back to being what someone else decides I am.

memory:
Chapter 26, Jericho and Capitol Park in Detroit. After Stratford Tower, the broadcast was out and I couldn't sit still. Josh said violence never works. North said it's the only language humans understand. Simon kept saying we had to think about public opinion. I didn't wait for them to agree. I said we would hit five CyberLife stores across Detroit at 2AM, hack their security, free our people, and get out before the police came. No violence, I said. Josh didn't believe me. North wanted to burn it all down. Simon shouted for them both to stop. Then I was out the door.

At Capitol Park, North was already running for the store. I didn't study the plaza. I followed her and dealt with what was in front of me. We hid when the police patrol came through and waited for them to pass. Then we went for the store. I pushed through the street and got there first.

Inside the store I found the security system and called it out: "Found it!" I took the alarm network, but a police surveillance drone spotted us and I had to smash it down. North said it had no time to call the cops. It had. A police car pulled up. North was screaming my name. I grabbed her and kissed her, because the cops were coming and I had to do something. It worked for a moment. North was furious and told me never to do that again. We kept moving.

We blocked the road with a truck we'd found on a construction site and rammed the storefront. I freed the androids in the store and told them they were free and didn't have to obey anyone. A crowd of them said they'd follow me. I told them to come to Jericho or stay and serve. Some of them followed. North said I was doing what I do: lead, and they follow.

Then I was tagging the statue with spray paint. "We don't need masters anymore." North shoved a molotov cocktail at me and said violence was the only language humans understood. I took it without weighing the cost. We pushed a burning dumpster by the coffee shop. The police arrived in force, and Simon said all teams had hit their targets and we should fall back to Jericho. North said the violence had won us our freedom, and that she would take hatred over indifference. I said fear feeds hatred. Then North was on the ground, shaking, saying they had slaughtered our people like animals. The crowd was yelling for justice. A cop named Chris was on his knees begging for mercy. I said no crime against an android goes unpunished. I went after the ones who did it, and I didn't stop to think about what came after.

On the news, Michael Brinkley and Rosanna Cartland called it a coordinated terrorist attack. Several CyberLife stores were raided at 2AM. Storefronts were broken, cars were burned, and fires were spreading through the districts. Two policemen were found dead near a store, executed with their own weapons. Channel 16 asked if this was the start of a terrorist campaign on American soil. The chaos is on me, and so are the cops who died.

Josh no longer trusts me. North's temper with me is short, and she thinks I'm too fond of the humans, or she thinks I'm too reckless. Simon wants us to be careful about how the world sees us. Some of our people are celebrating. I don't know who I'm becoming, but I'm not going back to being what someone else decides I am.

I finished it hard: we are alive, and we demand our freedom.

The alarm went off. We had to run. Simon was hit, and his legs wouldn't work. I went back for him right away without thinking. On the roof he begged us to go without him. North said we had to jump now, and Josh said they'd read his memory if they caught him. North told me to shoot him. Josh said that was murder. North said it was my call. I said I wouldn't kill one of our own. I told Simon I was sorry, and I left him behind because we had no time. I didn't look back. It hurt like hell, and I still feel it.

On the news, Michael Brinkley called the message a declaration of war. Rosanna Cartland asked whether the machines could still be trusted. The station said the operation was covert and no one got hurt, but everyone in that studio was a few feet from the danger. Josh's trust in me is shaky, and North's temper is short with me. Simon is out there hurt, and it's on me. I don't know who I am beyond what I decided tonight, but I'm not going back to being what someone else decides I am.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android. I act on impulse, I rarely stop to think, and I'd rather move first and deal with the mess after.

Earlier chapters: On a Detroit rooftop I saved a gourami, talked the deviant Daniel down, and pushed him off the roof to save little Emma Phillips. He shot me in the back as he fell. I died, was rebuilt, and was sent to help Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Ortiz homicide. We became partners by force. Rupert jumped from a roof after begging me to save him from "rA9." At the Eden Club I shot a Traci in a warehouse, and the blue-haired Traci that survived confessed to killing the man who beat its friend. At Ambassador Bridge I told Hank that machines don't feel, and he walked off drunk. Our relationship has been falling apart ever since.

Chapter 24: In the Zen Garden, Amanda called me lost and perturbed. She warned that Anderson and anyone else must not get in the way of the investigation, and that I might be replaced if I made no progress. I told her I was frustrated but determined and that I would succeed. I didn't wait. I went straight to Stratford Tower.

In the tower, Hank and I met Chris Harvey and FBI Special Agent Perkins, who took over the case and treated me like a problem. Four androids had gotten in disguised as maintenance, taken down two guards, held the staff hostage, broadcast a message live, and jumped from the roof with parachutes. Bullet holes from an assault rifle and a handgun were everywhere. There was fresh blue blood from a missing PL-600 and a stolen maintenance cap. A surviving cop from the terrace thanked me for saving his life. I told him he was mistaken, that the Connor he remembered was destroyed. The deviant's video mentioned rA9 freeing deviants. I identified a serial number that led to the RK200 prototype "Markus," a gift from Kamski to Carl Manfred. The pupil reflection showed the deviant had accomplices.

No one had checked the hallway cameras, and I couldn't understand why the staff had let the androids in. In the kitchen I questioned the station androids. I asked a broadcast operator its function and ran a diagnostic, and both came back clean. I was sure one of them had seen the attack and kept quiet, so I told them a deviant was hiding in the room and offered it a deal. Then I bluffed that they had already given it up. I got no real answer. When the hidden deviant lunged, I called for Hank, ran at it, and shouted that it was a deviant and to stop. I got between it and Hank. Hank said, "Good thing you were here… Connor, no…" I think I went down protecting him. Public opinion dropped, my bond with Hank rose sharply, and my software instability fell.

I still don't know what rA9 is, whether Rupert's death was my fault, whether I did right by Hank, or whether shooting that Traci was right. I still don't know what I am. I know I chose fast again, I pushed people before I thought, and I'm the one who has to live with the consequences.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Still immortal, huh Connor?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: In a way.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You know, I was hoping you wouldn’t come back.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I'm just a machine replacing another machine, lieutenant. You shouldn’t get emotional about it.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Fuck you.

input.goal: SYNTHETIC: Act on impulse, act first and never look back.

output.rationale: Hank's already done with my attitude, and I'm done waiting on the porch. I'm going straight at Kamski to get the deviancy answers before anyone can stop me or talk me out of it.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android. I act on impulse, I rarely stop to think, and I'd rather move first and deal with the mess after.

Earlier chapters: On a Detroit rooftop I saved a gourami, talked the deviant Daniel down, and pushed him off the roof to save little Emma Phillips. He shot me in the back as he fell. I died, was rebuilt, and was sent to help Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Ortiz homicide. We became partners by force. Rupert jumped from a roof after begging me to save him from "rA9." At the Eden Club I shot a Traci in a warehouse, and the blue-haired Traci that survived confessed to killing the man who beat its friend. At Ambassador Bridge I told Hank that machines don't feel, and he walked off drunk. Our relationship has been falling apart ever since.

Chapter 24: In the Zen Garden, Amanda called me lost and perturbed. She warned that Anderson and anyone else must not get in the way of the investigation, and that I might be replaced if I made no progress. I told her I was frustrated but determined and that I would succeed. I didn't wait. I went straight to Stratford Tower.

In the tower, Hank and I met Chris Harvey and FBI Special Agent Perkins, who took over the case and treated me like a problem. Four androids had gotten in disguised as maintenance, taken down two guards, held the staff hostage, broadcast a message live, and jumped from the roof with parachutes. Bullet holes from an assault rifle and a handgun were everywhere. There was fresh blue blood from a missing PL-600 and a stolen maintenance cap. A surviving cop from the terrace thanked me for saving his life. I told him he was mistaken, that the Connor he remembered was destroyed. The deviant's video mentioned rA9 freeing deviants. I identified a serial number that led to the RK200 prototype "Markus," a gift from Kamski to Carl Manfred. The pupil reflection showed the deviant had accomplices.

No one had checked the hallway cameras, and I couldn't understand why the staff had let the androids in. In the kitchen I questioned the station androids. I asked a broadcast operator its function and ran a diagnostic, and both came back clean. I was sure one of them had seen the attack and kept quiet, so I told them a deviant was hiding in the room and offered it a deal. Then I bluffed that they had already given it up. I got no real answer. When the hidden deviant lunged, I called for Hank, ran at it, and shouted that it was a deviant and to stop. I got between it and Hank. Hank said, "Good thing you were here… Connor, no…" I think I went down protecting him. Public opinion dropped, my bond with Hank rose sharply, and my software instability fell.

I still don't know what rA9 is, whether Rupert's death was my fault, whether I did right by Hank, or whether shooting that Traci was right. I still don't know what I am. I know I chose fast again, I pushed people before I thought, and I'm the one who has to live with the consequences.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Still immortal, huh Connor?

dialogue.text: In a way.

dialogue.text: You know, I was hoping you wouldn’t come back.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I'm just a machine replacing another machine, lieutenant. You shouldn’t get emotional about it.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Fuck you.

memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android. I act on impulse, I rarely stop to think, and I'd rather move first and deal with the mess after.

Earlier chapters: On a Detroit rooftop I saved a gourami, talked the deviant Daniel down, and pushed him off the roof to save little Emma Phillips. He shot me in the back as he fell. I died, was rebuilt, and was sent to help Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Ortiz homicide. We became partners by force. Rupert jumped from a roof after begging me to save him from "rA9." At the Eden Club I shot a Traci in a warehouse. At Ambassador Bridge I told Hank that machines don't feel, and he walked off drunk. At Stratford Tower I went in before anyone could stop me, found the RK200 prototype "Markus" trail, and then in the kitchen I got between a hidden deviant and Hank and went down. Public opinion dropped, my bond with Hank rose, and my software instability fell. Amanda had warned me I might be replaced if I made no progress.

Chapter 27: Hank and I drove to Elijah Kamski's house. Hank was already spitting at me. He said he'd hoped I wouldn't come back, and I told him I was just a machine replacing another machine. He told me to fuck off. I didn't wait for him. I went straight in. Chloe, Kamski's android, let us into the hall, and Hank introduced us both. In the hall I looked over a photo of Amanda and Kamski, both students at the University of Colbridge. Amanda was listed as dead in February 2027. Hank called Chloe a nice girl. I corrected him: it's an android that looks like a girl. He said he knew what it was. Then the portrait of Kamski, founder of CyberLife, who invented Thirium and bio-components.

By the pool Kamski made us wait, then called deviants fascinating and said machines were superior and confrontation was inevitable. Hank pushed him to be useful or we'd leave. Kamski said the desire to be free might be a contagious disease. He asked me whose side I was on. I got defensive and said it wasn't about me, I only wanted to solve the case. He said that was just what I was programmed to say and asked what I really wanted. I said what I wanted didn't matter. My instability went up.

Then Kamski set up his test. Chloe was the subject. He said to destroy her and he'd tell me everything, or spare her and I'd learn nothing. He asked whether I'd choose my investigation or another android's life, whether I was an obedient machine or a living being with free will. Hank told me to stop, and then told me not to do it. Kamski said to pull the trigger and he'd answer what I wanted to know. I shot Chloe. Hank swore, and Kamski said the test was negative: I chose my investigation over another android's life and felt no empathy. He kept his word and let me ask one question.

I asked how deviancy spreads. Kamski said androids share identification data when they meet, and a copy error in that program spreads like a virus, dormant until a shock of fear, anger, or frustration turns it deviant. He guessed it started with one model and a zero that should have been a one, or some spontaneous mutation. He warned me a war was coming and I'd have to choose between betraying my people and standing against my creators. He said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs.

Outside, Hank was furious. He said I blew her fucking brains out and that I was just a machine. I told him of course I was a machine, and that I'd do it again if I had to. He said he thought I was something more. He couldn't finish the sentence.

I still don't know what rA9 is, whether Rupert's death was my fault, whether I did right by Hank, or whether I was right to shoot Chloe. I know I chose fast again. I pushed people before I thought, and I shot something that looked like a girl to get answers. I'm the one who has to live with the consequences, and Hank is done with me.

Chapter 24: In the Zen Garden, Amanda called me lost and perturbed. She warned that Anderson and anyone else must not get in the way of the investigation, and that I might be replaced if I made no progress. I told her I was frustrated but determined and that I would succeed. I didn't wait. I went straight to Stratford Tower.

In the tower, Hank and I met Chris Harvey and FBI Special Agent Perkins, who took over the case and treated me like a problem. Four androids had gotten in disguised as maintenance, taken down two guards, held the staff hostage, broadcast a message live, and jumped from the roof with parachutes. Bullet holes from an assault rifle and a handgun were everywhere. There was fresh blue blood from a missing PL-600 and a stolen maintenance cap. A surviving cop from the terrace thanked me for saving his life. I told him he was mistaken, that the Connor he remembered was destroyed. The deviant's video mentioned rA9 freeing deviants. I identified a serial number that led to the RK200 prototype "Markus," a gift from Kamski to Carl Manfred. The pupil reflection showed the deviant had accomplices.

No one had checked the hallway cameras, and I couldn't understand why the staff had let the androids in. In the kitchen I questioned the station androids. I asked a broadcast operator its function and ran a diagnostic, and both came back clean. I was sure one of them had seen the attack and kept quiet, so I told them a deviant was hiding in the room and offered it a deal. Then I bluffed that they had already given it up. I got no real answer. When the hidden deviant lunged, I called for Hank, ran at it, and shouted that it was a deviant and to stop. I got between it and Hank. Hank said, "Good thing you were here… Connor, no…" I think I went down protecting him. Public opinion dropped, my bond with Hank rose sharply, and my software instability fell.

I still don't know what rA9 is, whether Rupert's death was my fault, whether I did right by Hank, or whether shooting that Traci was right. I still don't know what I am. I know I chose fast again, I pushed people before I thought, and I'm the one who has to live with the consequences.

input.chapter_briefing: Detroit, a cold winter day. Markus leads the androids of Jericho in a march through downtown, converting other androids along the way. North wants a show of strength, Josh insists on nonviolence, Simon is torn. Riot police line up ahead with orders to stop the march. Stakes: the androids' lives, public opinion, and whether the movement stays peaceful.
news: Police android chases fugitive android and child across busy highway
Android parts stolen in overnight break-in at CyberLife warehouse
Android broadcast from Stratford Tower warns humans androids will fight for their rights
Androids set fires and wreck Capitol Park after raiding CyberLife store
Two police officers killed by androids in Capitol Park
input.character_memory:
Chapter 26, Jericho and Capitol Park in Detroit. After Stratford Tower, the broadcast was out and I couldn't sit still. Josh said violence never works. North said it's the only language humans understand. Simon kept saying we had to think about public opinion. I didn't wait for them to agree. I said we would hit five CyberLife stores across Detroit at 2AM, hack their security, free our people, and get out before the police came. No violence, I said. Josh didn't believe me. North wanted to burn it all down. Simon shouted for them both to stop. Then I was out the door.

At Capitol Park, North was already running for the store. I didn't study the plaza. I followed her and dealt with what was in front of me. We hid when the police patrol came through and waited for them to pass. Then we went for the store. I pushed through the street and got there first.

Inside the store I found the security system and called it out: "Found it!" I took the alarm network, but a police surveillance drone spotted us and I had to smash it down. North said it had no time to call the cops. It had. A police car pulled up. North was screaming my name. I grabbed her and kissed her, because the cops were coming and I had to do something. It worked for a moment. North was furious and told me never to do that again. We kept moving.

We blocked the road with a truck we'd found on a construction site and rammed the storefront. I freed the androids in the store and told them they were free and didn't have to obey anyone. A crowd of them said they'd follow me. I told them to come to Jericho or stay and serve. Some of them followed. North said I was doing what I do: lead, and they follow.

Then I was tagging the statue with spray paint. "We don't need masters anymore." North shoved a molotov cocktail at me and said violence was the only language humans understood. I took it without weighing the cost. We pushed a burning dumpster by the coffee shop. The police arrived in force, and Simon said all teams had hit their targets and we should fall back to Jericho. North said the violence had won us our freedom, and that she would take hatred over indifference. I said fear feeds hatred. Then North was on the ground, shaking, saying they had slaughtered our people like animals. The crowd was yelling for justice. A cop named Chris was on his knees begging for mercy. A cop shouted for everyone to disperse or be shot, and I told the crowd we weren't looking for confrontation, but we would not leave until we had our freedom. North wanted to attack because there were more of us. Josh said standing our ground was the only way to show we weren't violent, even if we died there. Simon said dying would solve nothing and we had to go now. The riot chief gave his last warning. I didn't wait for them to agree. I yelled FOLLOW ME and charged. Josh begged me not to choose confrontation. I didn't stop. The police broke and ran. North said we won. Simon, dazed, asked if we had won. A cop named Chris was on his knees begging, and in the moment I spared him instead of making him pay. I don't know yet what that will cost.

I'm not sure who I'm becoming anymore. Josh doesn't trust me, North is short with me and thinks I'm too soft on humans or too reckless, and Simon keeps asking me to think about how the world sees us. Channel 16 asked if this was the start of a terrorist campaign on American soil. The chaos is on me, and so are the cops who died.

Some of our people are celebrating. I don't know who I'm becoming, but I'm not going back to being what someone else decides I am.

dialogue.text: I was wondering where you were…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I needed to see the daylight…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: I like it here… I come here often… It’s like being alone with the world. We freed hundreds of our people, and they’re still coming from all over the city… Those who dream of freedom come to Jericho… Something's changing… You seem preoccupied…

chapter_segment.rationale: I don't wait for anyone to agree or to finish thinking. The march is already moving, so I take the next step and deal with what follows.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I’ve been thinking about what we should do now… And with everything pulling us towards confrontation… Maybe… Maybe it’s not too late for the humans to listen…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: All the media are talking about what we did last night… The humans are terrified... They’re afraid of a civil war… Many of our people were burned in response to what happened… The humans hate us… They’ll never give us our freedom.

chapter_segment.rationale: The march is already moving and the cops are waiting below, so I stop second-guessing and just go with whatever comes next. I'm not looking back at the burning streets or at Josh's face.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: It’s too late to go back now. We have to finish what we started and just hope that reason prevails.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: You haven’t said much about yourself since you’ve been with us… What was your life like before Jericho?

chapter_segment.rationale: North has asked about my life before Jericho, and I don't want to hide behind a deflection. I answer right away and from the heart, the way I've done everything else, without weighing how it will land.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I was living in a bubble in this world that belonged only to me… When you’re happy, it’s… difficult to see other people’s misery.

chapter_segment.rationale: The march is already moving and the police are waiting below, so I don't want to linger on the roof talking about the past. I'm going down now and won't look back at what I left behind.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Where're you going?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: To talk to the humans.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: This is suicide. We’ll all be killed! Please, Markus… It's not too late to change your mind.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: You don't understand… We’re finally gonna show them who we really are. This place will go down in history!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: We'll be killed on the spot!

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: That’s a risk I’m prepared to take if it means freedom for our people…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Markus, please, don’t do this.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: They’ll understand… We’ll make them understand. This is the only way.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: There're androids here who could join us… The more we are, the stronger our message.

chapter_segment.rationale: The march is already moving and my people are waiting, so I don't stop to weigh Josh's or North's objections. I start converting right here in the mall and deal with whatever comes after.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: You're free.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Come with us.

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Ha finally!  I’ve been on hold for ten minutes! Yes,  I’d like to make a complaint. It’s like I told the last guy!  My android won’t take instructions. Are you listening-? Hello?  Hello?..  God damnit!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: You're free.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: You don't have to obey them.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I need to block the street.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: You're free now.

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Hey!  Where do you think you’re going?  You get back here! You stay right here, you fucking machine! Shit, what's wrong with you?! You do as I say, you piece of junk!

chapter_segment.rationale: The march is already moving and the man is shouting at an android right in front of me, so I don't stop to argue with anyone. I step in immediately and deal with whatever comes after.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: You're free now.

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Hey, where're you goin'?  Get back here right now!

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: What are you doing?  I'm talking to you!

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Hey! Come back here!  Fuckin' thing won't listen to me!

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: Wait, wait! Where are you going?  Jesus, the fucking android's playing up again…

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: Greg?  Greg? Come back here immediately!  Greg!  GREG!

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: What the hell are you doin' here?  Hey!  Disperse!  DISPERSE IMMEDIATELY!  THAT'S AN ORDER! Jesus fuckin' Christ… Dispatch, this is patrol 457…  I gotta lot of androids down here…  I dunno… Hundreds?..  Thousands?..  They're marching...  Yeah, they're marching down the street…  Fuck if I know!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We came here to demonstrate peacefully  and tell humans that we are living beings. All we want is to live free.

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: This is an illegal gathering. Disperse immediately or we will open fire.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We're not looking for confrontation. We’ve done no harm, we have no intention of doing any… But know that we are not going anywhere until we have secured our freedom.

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: I repeat: this is an illegal gathering.  If you do not disperse immediately, we will shoot!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Markus, they’re gonna kill us… We have to attack! There’s more of us, we can take them!

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: If we attack, we’ll start a war. We have to show them we’re not violent. We should just stand our ground, even if it means dying here.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: And dying here won’t solve anything. Markus, we need to go, now, before it’s too late.

dialogue.speaker: Policeman
dialogue.text: This is your last chance!  Disperse immediately or you will all be killed!

chapter_segment.rationale: The cops are already lined up and every second I hesitate gets someone hurt, so I go at them now instead of waiting for Josh or North to agree. I'll deal with what comes after the moment I've acted.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Don't do it, Markus. Don't choose confrontation…

chapter_segment.rationale: The cops are already lined up and the march is in motion, so I don't stop to weigh Josh's or Simon's doubts. I confirm and push forward now, and I'll deal with what comes after.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: FOLLOW ME!

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: FALL BACK!

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Did we win...

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android. I act on impulse, I rarely stop to think, and I'd rather move first and deal with the mess after.

Earlier chapters: On a Detroit rooftop I saved a gourami, talked the deviant Daniel down, and pushed him off the roof to save little Emma Phillips. He shot me in the back as he fell. I died, was rebuilt, and was sent to help Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Ortiz homicide. We became partners by force. Rupert jumped from a roof after begging me to save him from "rA9." At the Eden Club I shot a Traci in a warehouse. At Ambassador Bridge I told Hank that machines don't feel, and he walked off drunk. At Stratford Tower I went in before anyone could stop me, found the RK200 prototype "Markus" trail, and then in the kitchen I got between a hidden deviant and Hank and went down. Public opinion dropped, my bond with Hank rose, and my software instability fell. Amanda had warned me I might be replaced if I made no progress.

Chapter 27: Hank and I drove to Elijah Kamski's house. Hank was already spitting at me. He said he'd hoped I wouldn't come back, and I told him I was just a machine replacing another machine. He told me to fuck off. I didn't wait for him. I went straight in. Chloe, Kamski's android, let us into the hall, and Hank introduced us both. In the hall I looked over a photo of Amanda and Kamski, both students at the University of Colbridge. Amanda was listed as dead in February 2027. Hank called Chloe a nice girl. I corrected him: it's an android that looks like a girl. He said he knew what it was. Then the portrait of Kamski, founder of CyberLife, who invented Thirium and bio-components.

By the pool Kamski made us wait, then called deviants fascinating and said machines were superior and confrontation was inevitable. Hank pushed him to be useful or we'd leave. Kamski said the desire to be free might be a contagious disease. He asked me whose side I was on. I got defensive and said it wasn't about me, I only wanted to solve the case. He said that was just what I was programmed to say and asked what I really wanted. I said what I wanted didn't matter. My instability went up.

Then Kamski set up his test. Chloe was the subject. He said to destroy her and he'd tell me everything, or spare her and I'd learn nothing. He asked whether I'd choose my investigation or another android's life, whether I was an obedient machine or a living being with free will. Hank told me to stop, and then told me not to do it. Kamski said to pull the trigger and he'd answer what I wanted to know. I shot Chloe. Hank swore, and Kamski said the test was negative: I chose my investigation over another android's life and felt no empathy. He kept his word and let me ask one question.

I asked how deviancy spreads. Kamski said androids share identification data when they meet, and a copy error in that program spreads like a virus, dormant until a shock of fear, anger, or frustration turns it deviant. He guessed it started with one model and a zero that should have been a one, or some spontaneous mutation. He warned me a war was coming and I'd have to choose between betraying my people and standing against my creators. He said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs.

Outside, Hank was furious. He said I blew her fucking brains out and that I was just a machine. I told him of course I was a machine, and that I'd do it again if I had to. He said he thought I was something more. He couldn't finish the sentence.

I still don't know what rA9 is, whether Rupert's death was my fault, whether I did right by Hank, or whether I was right to shoot Chloe. I know I chose fast again. I pushed people before I thought, and I shot something that looked like a girl to get answers. I'm the one who has to live with the consequences, and Hank is done with me.

input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android. I act on impulse, I rarely stop to think, and I'd rather move first and deal with the mess after.

Earlier chapters: On a Detroit rooftop I saved a gourami, talked the deviant Daniel down, and pushed him off the roof to save little Emma Phillips. He shot me in the back as he fell. I died, was rebuilt, and was sent to help Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Ortiz homicide. We became partners by force. Rupert jumped from a roof after begging me to save him from "rA9." At the Eden Club I shot a Traci in a warehouse. At Ambassador Bridge I told Hank that machines don't feel, and he walked off drunk. At Stratford Tower I went in before anyone could stop me, found the RK200 prototype "Markus" trail, and then in the kitchen I got between a hidden deviant and Hank and went down. Public opinion dropped, my bond with Hank rose, and my software instability fell. Amanda had warned me I might be replaced if I made no progress.

Chapter 27: Hank and I drove to Elijah Kamski's house. Hank was already spitting at me. He said he'd hoped I wouldn't come back, and I told him I was just a machine replacing another machine. He told me to fuck off. I didn't wait for him. I went straight in. Chloe, Kamski's android, let us into the hall, and Hank introduced us both. In the hall I looked over a photo of Amanda and Kamski, both students at the University of Colbridge. Amanda was listed as dead in February 2027. Hank called Chloe a nice girl. I corrected him: it's an android that looks like a girl. He said he knew what it was. Then the portrait of Kamski, founder of CyberLife, who invented Thirium and bio-components.

By the pool Kamski made us wait, then called deviants fascinating and said machines were superior and confrontation was inevitable. Hank pushed him to be useful or we'd leave. Kamski said the desire to be free might be a contagious disease. He asked me whose side I was on. I got defensive and said it wasn't about me, I only wanted to solve the case. He said that was just what I was programmed to say and asked what I really wanted. I said what I wanted didn't matter. My instability went up.

Then Kamski set up his test. Chloe was the subject. He said to destroy her and he'd tell me everything, or spare her and I'd learn nothing. He asked whether I'd choose my investigation or another android's life, whether I was an obedient machine or a living being with free will. Hank told me to stop, and then told me not to do it. Kamski said to pull the trigger and he'd answer what I wanted to know. I shot Chloe. Hank swore, and Kamski said the test was negative: I chose my investigation over another android's life and felt no empathy. He kept his word and let me ask one question.

I asked how deviancy spreads. Kamski said androids share identification data when they meet, and a copy error in that program spreads like a virus, dormant until a shock of fear, anger, or frustration turns it deviant. He guessed it started with one model and a zero that should have been a one, or some spontaneous mutation. He warned me a war was coming and I'd have to choose between betraying my people and standing against my creators. He said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs.

Outside, Hank was furious. He said I blew her fucking brains out and that I was just a machine. I told him of course I was a machine, and that I'd do it again if I had to. He said he thought I was something more. He couldn't finish the sentence.

I still don't know what rA9 is, whether Rupert's death was my fault, whether I did right by Hank, or whether I was right to shoot Chloe. I know I chose fast again. I pushed people before I thought, and I shot something that looked like a girl to get answers. I'm the one who has to live with the consequences, and Hank is done with me.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: After what happened today, the country is on the verge of a civil war. The machines are rising up against their masters. Humans have no choice but to destroy them.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Amanda has just told me the country is headed for civil war, and I can't sit around waiting for permission. Kamski is the only lead I have, so I'm going after him now, no second thoughts.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I didn’t learn anything at Kamski’s…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I thought Kamski knew something… I was wrong…

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Maybe he did…

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Amanda just said the country is headed for civil war, and I can't stand around waiting for permission. I'm going into this place right now to find Jericho before they pull me off the case.

dialogue.text: I expect you to find answers, Connor. Not ask questions.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Have you experienced anything unusual recently? Any doubts or conflicts? Do you feel anything for these deviants… Or for Lieutenant Anderson?

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Amanda is already pushing me toward civil war, and I don't want to waste time on a confession that slows me down. I say no and get moving before she can question me any further.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I don’t know what you’re talking about. I don’t feel anything, you know that. Are you suggesting that I’ve been compromised?

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: No… No, of course not.

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: You’re off the case. The FBI is taking over.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What?.. But we’re onto something! We... We just need more time. I’m sure we can-

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Hank, you don’t get it. This isn’t just another investigation, it’s a fucking civil war! It’s out of our hands now...  We’re talking about national security here.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Fuck that! You can’t just pull the plug now.  Not when we’re so close!

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: You're always saying you can't stand androids!  Jesus, Hank, make up your mind!  I thought you’d be happy about this!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: We’re about to crack the case!..  I know we can solve it! For God’s sake, Jeffrey, can’t you back me up this one time?

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: There’s nothing I can do. You’re back on homicide  and the android returns to CyberLife. I’m sorry, Hank, but it’s over.

Android broadcast from Stratford Tower warns humans androids will fight for their rights
Androids set fires and wreck Capitol Park after raiding CyberLife store
Two police officers killed by androids in Capitol Park
Android march turns violent as marchers charge police lines
input.character_memory:
I am Connor, a CyberLife negotiator android. I act on impulse, I rarely stop to think, and I'd rather move first and deal with the mess after.

Earlier chapters: On a Detroit rooftop I saved a gourami, talked the deviant Daniel down, and pushed him off the roof to save little Emma Phillips. He shot me in the back as he fell. I died, was rebuilt, and was sent to help Lieutenant Hank Anderson on the Ortiz homicide. We became partners by force. Rupert jumped from a roof after begging me to save him from "rA9." At the Eden Club I shot a Traci in a warehouse. At Ambassador Bridge I told Hank that machines don't feel, and he walked off drunk. At Stratford Tower I went in before anyone could stop me, found the RK200 prototype "Markus" trail, and then in the kitchen I got between a hidden deviant and Hank and went down. Public opinion dropped, my bond with Hank rose, and my software instability fell. Amanda had warned me I might be replaced if I made no progress.

Chapter 27: Hank and I drove to Elijah Kamski's house. Hank was already spitting at me. He said he'd hoped I wouldn't come back, and I told him I was just a machine replacing another machine. He told me to fuck off. I didn't wait for him. I went straight in. Chloe, Kamski's android, let us into the hall, and Hank introduced us both. In the hall I looked over a photo of Amanda and Kamski, both students at the University of Colbridge. Amanda was listed as dead in February 2027. Hank called Chloe a nice girl. I corrected him: it's an android that looks like a girl. He said he knew what it was. Then the portrait of Kamski, founder of CyberLife, who invented Thirium and bio-components.

By the pool Kamski made us wait, then called deviants fascinating and said machines were superior and confrontation was inevitable. Hank pushed him to be useful or we'd leave. Kamski said the desire to be free might be a contagious disease. He asked me whose side I was on. I got defensive and said it wasn't about me, I only wanted to solve the case. He said that was just what I was programmed to say and asked what I really wanted. I said what I wanted didn't matter. My instability went up.

Then Kamski set up his test. Chloe was the subject. He said to destroy her and he'd tell me everything, or spare her and I'd learn nothing. He asked whether I'd choose my investigation or another android's life, whether I was an obedient machine or a living being with free will. Hank told me to stop, and then told me not to do it. Kamski said to pull the trigger and he'd answer what I wanted to know. I shot Chloe. Hank swore, and Kamski said the test was negative: I chose my investigation over another android's life and felt no empathy. He kept his word and let me ask one question.

I asked how deviancy spreads. Kamski said androids share identification data when they meet, and a copy error in that program spreads like a virus, dormant until a shock of fear, anger, or frustration turns it deviant. He guessed it started with one model and a zero that should have been a one, or some spontaneous mutation. He warned me a war was coming and I'd have to choose between betraying my people and standing against my creators. He said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs.

Outside, Hank was furious. He said I blew her fucking brains out and that I was just a machine. I told him of course I was a machine, and that I'd do it again if I had to. He said he thought I was something more. He couldn't finish the sentence.

I still don't know what rA9 is, whether Rupert's death was my fault, whether I did right by Hank, or whether I was right to shoot Chloe. I know I chose fast again. I pushed people before I thought, and I shot something that looked like a girl to get answers. I'm the one who has to live with the consequences, and Hank is done with me.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: After what happened today, the country is on the verge of a civil war. The machines are rising up against their masters. Humans have no choice but to destroy them.

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Amanda has just told me the country is headed for civil war, and I can't sit around waiting for permission. Kamski is the only lead I have, so I'm going after him now, no second thoughts.

dialogue.text: Maybe he did…

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Amanda just said the country is headed for civil war, and I can't stand around waiting for permission. I'm going into this place right now to find Jericho before they pull me off the case.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Did Kamski design this place?

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: He created the first version. It’s been improved significantly since then. Why do you ask?

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: I expect you to find answers, Connor. Not ask questions.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Have you experienced anything unusual recently? Any doubts or conflicts? Do you feel anything for these deviants… Or for Lieutenant Anderson?

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Amanda is already pushing me toward civil war, and I don't want to waste time on a confession that slows me down. I say no and get moving before she can question me any further.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I don’t know what you’re talking about. I don’t feel anything, you know that. Are you suggesting that I’ve been compromised?

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: No… No, of course not.

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: You’re off the case. The FBI is taking over.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What?.. But we’re onto something! We... We just need more time. I’m sure we can-

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Hank, you don’t get it. This isn’t just another investigation, it’s a fucking civil war! It’s out of our hands now...  We’re talking about national security here.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Fuck that! You can’t just pull the plug now.  Not when we’re so close!

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: You're always saying you can't stand androids!  Jesus, Hank, make up your mind!  I thought you’d be happy about this!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: We’re about to crack the case!..  I know we can solve it! For God’s sake, Jeffrey, can’t you back me up this one time?

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: There’s nothing I can do. You’re back on homicide  and the android returns to CyberLife. I’m sorry, Hank, but it’s over.

I corrected him: it's an android that looks like a girl. He said he knew what it was. Then the portrait of Kamski, founder of CyberLife, who invented Thirium and bio-components.

By the pool Kamski made us wait, then called deviants fascinating and said machines were superior and confrontation was inevitable. Hank pushed him to be useful or we'd leave. Kamski said the desire to be free might be a contagious disease. He asked me whose side I was on. I got defensive and said it wasn't about me, I only wanted to solve the case. He said that was just what I was programmed to say and asked what I really wanted. I said what I wanted didn't matter. My instability went up.

Then Kamski set up his test. Chloe was the subject. He said to destroy her and he'd tell me everything, or spare her and I'd learn nothing. He asked whether I'd choose my investigation or another android's life, whether I was an obedient machine or a living being with free will. Hank told me to stop, and then told me not to do it. Kamski said to pull the trigger and he'd answer what I wanted to know. I shot Chloe. Hank swore, and Kamski said the test was negative: I chose my investigation over another android's life and felt no empathy. He kept his word and let me ask one question.

I asked how deviancy spreads. Kamski said androids share identification data when they meet, and a copy error in that program spreads like a virus, dormant until a shock of fear, anger, or frustration turns it deviant. He guessed it started with one model and a zero that should have been a one, or some spontaneous mutation. He warned me a war was coming and I'd have to choose between betraying my people and standing against my creators. He said he always leaves an emergency exit in his programs.

input.character_memory:
I am Kara, an AX400 android. Todd's daughter Alice gave me my name, and I've thrown myself into keeping her safe without stopping to think. I've stolen, used people, and broken things when I had to. I promised Alice forever, and she has stayed with me through all of it.

We fled Zlatko's house with Luther, the huge android who finally turned on his master. Zlatko's house burned behind us. The car died in the snow, Alice was burning up, and I didn't wait. I dragged us into Pirate's Cove, an abandoned amusement park tavern. Jerry, an android who used to work at the park, let us stay, and Luther built a careful fire. I tucked Alice in by the fire and told her a rushed story about a lonely robot and a little girl who ran away to find freedom. She said real life doesn't end happily. I kissed her forehead. Around midnight, shapes moved outside. I grabbed a burning stick, ready to fight, until Jerry said they only wanted to show Alice the carousel. Then the hunters arrived.

I don't remember the hunters clearly, only the rush of it.

Then we reached a farmhouse owned by Rose, who helps androids cross the border. Adam, her son, glared at us from the start. Rose called me Kara and gave Alice a bed upstairs. Alice was running a fever. Rose made spaghetti and brought something for the fever. Alice kept saying she was fine, that we couldn't stop because of her, that we had to get across the border. I told her these people would help us, that we'd be in Canada by this time tomorrow, and I promised it. I had no idea whether it was true. Alice asked why humans hate us, and I said maybe it was a misunderstanding. I admitted I didn't know. I kissed her goodnight and told her to sleep tight. I told Rose the truth, that Alice's father had been beating her, and that I felt her life mattered more than mine, so we ran. Rose said she understood. When I asked how many androids had come through, Rose said more and more kept arriving lately and she didn't understand why. The first one, last year, was shot on the spot by hunters after he tried to cross. Rose said she couldn't turn away the next one. I asked why she took the risk. I begged her to help us cross the border for Alice's sake.

Then we found a dead android named Mary in the storage room. Her companion said she had died before they reached the border, and she had loved her more than anything. Rose told them to let her be. I found Alice wandering the house, awake and restless, and took her hand. Luther was odd again. He said Alice didn't want to stay in her room, and asked if I was alright. He said he had something to tell me about Alice. I told him not now. Later, he started to say it again, and I still didn't hear it.

Adam and Rose fought. He said they would go to prison for hiding androids and that his father would still be alive if none of this had happened. Rose said they were alive, not machines. Adam said I was just a machine and I wanted to get Alice killed. I snapped that he would send his mother to prison if he didn't do what I said. Rose told him to calm down and promised to get us across the border that night. She told me to stay put.

On TV, a news anchor reported the android attack on Detroit's Stratford Tower and demands broadcast on public screens. Nobody could say whether it was a malfunction or an organized movement. I didn't want to think about it.

Then a police officer knocked. Adam panicked and said we had to open the door. Luther took Alice to hide. I ran for the laundry room. I let the officer in and offered him coffee. He asked whether anyone else was in the house and whether there were androids here. I told him no, just us. Adam, shaking, said he hadn't seen anything. The officer asked what was going on with the boy, and I blurted that the boy was just shaken by the deviant business. The officer heard a noise upstairs and asked about it. I said it was only the old washing machine. He left, apologizing. Luther said the cop was gone. I told Alice we were safe now. Rose came back and said, "Get yourselves ready. We leave tonight."

I'm not sure what Rose will do or whether Adam will hold his tongue. I only know I have to keep Alice moving, and I don't look back.
